newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian call money ends lower, gilt prices mixed.
newsitem.headline: Indian call money ends lower, gilt prices mixed.

text.p: Indian call money rates eased on an increased supply of funds to end Wednesday in the 5.0-5.5 percent range, off the day's high of 6.5, dealers said.
Call money opened the day at 5.5-6.25 percent.
Dealers said rates eased in the afternoon as funds supply improved on account of repayment of loans towards food procurement operations.
"The repayment led to an inflow of funds into the banking system," said a dealer at a state-run bank. "This eased rates."
Dealers said prices of government securities ended mixed in moderate trade.
Traded volumes on the National Stock Exchange improved to 1.5 billion rupees from 1.32 on Tuesday, they said.

The 13.50 percent 1997 government of India stock traded on Wednesday at 103.05 rupees against its last traded price of 103.18 while the 13.65 percent 1999 stock traded at102.23 rupees against 102.25, dealers said.
Treasury bills with April maturity traded on Wednesday at a yield of 7.45 percent against 7.25 percent.
